About me

I’m currently a second year master’s student in engineering physics at the University of Liège, Belgium. My interests are numerical methods and computational physics, especially for continuum mechanics.

My past projects include:

  • a particle-in-cell code for inviscid fluids, for both internal and free-surface flows, which you can read more about in the portfolio,
  • a FDTD solver for the simulation of electromagnetic waves, with an emphasis on high-performance computing (OpenMP, MPI, CUDA),
  • experimental research on transparent conducting materials, more specifically on TiO2\mathrm{TiO}_2TiO2​ coatings on silver nanowire networks, under the supervision of Pr. Ngoc Duy Nguyen.

My master’s thesis will be linked to the PFEM2 method, under the supervision of Pr. Jean-Philippe Ponthot and Pr. Romain Boman.
